notes.type_correctness: All function signatures are correct: PieceRenderer.update(state, elapsedSec=0) is backward-compatible, ShakeEffect.tick/reset/triggerShake types are sound, ColorMatrixFilter imported from 'pixi.js' directly (v8 path confirmed by successful build). The tetrisFlashOverlay.filters cast to import('pixi.js').Filter[] is a minor type workaround but compiles cleanly.
notes.pattern_adherence: ShakeEffect follows the same renderer-module ownership pattern as PostProcessController: instantiated in main.ts, passed app.stage. Combo tracking correctly lives in main.ts (only file that sees both action buffer and event stream). All pre-allocation patterns match the existing particle pool approach. One minor deviation: the sweep-flash Graphics are created dynamically per-clear (not pooled), consistent with the previous implementation.
notes.test_coverage: 12 new tests cover EffectsRenderer: pool size, piece-lock burst, edge pulse scaling (counts 1/2/3), Tetris flash (count=4), level-up overlays, tick drain, and shimmer phase. Gaps: no test for ShakeEffect class (triggerShake/reset/tick not unit-tested), no test for combo ripple ring activation, no test for chromatic aberration overlay. These are non-blocking but noted.
notes.security: Pure canvas rendering code with no network I/O, DOM manipulation, or user input parsing. No attack surface introduced.
notes.architectural_alignment: Zero engine modifications confirmed. Import boundaries clean: shakeEffect.ts imports only 'pixi.js' Container; effects.ts imports only from engine/ (types, board, rotation, pieces, gameState) and renderer/ (boardRenderer). main.ts remains the sole cross-layer importer. Chroma/ripple overlays correctly placed in screenContainer (effectsContainer in main.ts), not boardContainer.
